clue.text: Simplistic account contained in dossier

indicators.note: contained in says the account abbreviation sits inside the word for dossier

parts.note: a dossier is a file of papers

explanation.surface: A critic dismisses an oversimplified report tucked into an intelligence file.
explanation.definitionFit: Facile describes an argument or answer that is superficial and too easily reached, the same as simplistic.

clue.text: Supply vital input to support informative response

parts.note: to feed is to supply something with the input it needs, such as fuel or food
to back is to support

explanation.surface: Contributing key ideas to a project in order to back it up.
explanation.definitionFit: Feedback is information given in response to something, used to assess or improve it.

clue.text: What could be nicely defined, top or bottom, by radius

definitions.text: What could be nicely defined, top or bottom, by radius

indicators.note: what could be signals that these letters could be rearranged into the answer
top or bottom picks the end letter of defined, and its first and last letters are both D

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for radius in geometry

explanation.surface: A geometry description: a shape whose top and bottom circles are neatly fixed by a radius.
explanation.walkthrough: Defined starts and ends with D, so either 'top or bottom' gives the same letter; NICELY, D and R rearranged give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A right circular cylinder has identical circular ends, each completely fixed by its radius.

clue.text: Mooched about, stopping to idle aimlessly

indicators.note: stopping means plugging, so the word for about fills a gap in the scrambled letters
aimlessly means the letters of to idle wander into a new order

parts.note: re means about, concerning

explanation.surface: Someone wandered around, pausing just to laze without purpose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mooched about' looks like the definition, but 'about' gives RE, which goes into LOITED, the anagram of TO IDLE.
explanation.definitionFit: To mooch is to hang around idly or aimlessly, the same as loitering.

clue.text: Aggressive speech managed to stop Major's replacement

indicators.note: to stop means the word for managed plugs the gap inside the replacement's name

parts.note: William Hague replaced John Major as leader of the UK Conservative Party in 1997
ran, as in ran a business, means managed

explanation.surface: A furious tirade is delivered to prevent a senior army officer being succeeded.
explanation.walkthrough: Major looks like a military rank, but it is John Major, British prime minister until 1997; his successor as Tory leader was William Hague.
explanation.definitionFit: A harangue is a lengthy, forceful and aggressive lecture or tirade.

clue.text: Lingering symptom of consumption?

parts.note: consumption suggests the old name for tuberculosis, but here it is eating or drinking, whose effect lingers on the tongue

explanation.walkthrough: Consumption was the common old name for tuberculosis, so the clue seems medical; the question mark flags that it means eating instead.
explanation.definitionFit: The flavour that stays in the mouth after food or drink has been swallowed.

clue.text: Expert in origin of transistor radio's development

indicators.note: development means the letters are worked up into a new arrangement

parts.note: the word radio, its possessive ending treated as a link

indicators.note: origin of means the first letter of transistor

explanation.surface: A specialist in how the transistor radio came about.
explanation.definitionFit: Adroit means skilful and clever, so expert used as an adjective.

clue.text: Instrument starts to generate useful information through automated reasoning

indicators.note: starts to means take the opening letter of each of the following six words

explanation.surface: A tool begins producing helpful data by means of machine logic.
explanation.definitionFit: A guitar is a stringed musical instrument.

clue.text: Wagner's first to abandon important scores

indicators.note: to abandon means the composer's initial is left out of the longer word

parts.note: weighty means important, significant

indicators.note: first means just the opening letter of the composer's name

explanation.surface: The composer Wagner gives up on his significant musical scores.
explanation.walkthrough: Scores looks like sheet music beside Wagner, but a score is twenty.
explanation.definitionFit: A score is twenty, so four scores make this number; the plural stands for several twenties together.

clue.text: Half-fat jams spoilt rice cake

indicators.note: jams means wedges in, so half the fat word is forced into the middle of the scrambled letters
spoilt means the letters of rice are messed up and rearranged
half signals that only the first two letters of the four-letter fat word are used

parts.note: lard is cooking fat

explanation.surface: A dieter's half-fat jam has ruined a rice cake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spoilt' rearranges RICE into EC...IR, and 'jams' wedges LA, the first half of LARD, between them.
explanation.definitionFit: An eclair is a finger-shaped choux pastry cake filled with cream and topped with chocolate.

clue.text: Authentic report of sizeable Scottish settlement

indicators.note: report of means what is heard spoken, so the place name is taken by its sound

parts.note: Stirling is a city in central Scotland

explanation.surface: A genuine account of a large town in Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Sterling, of silver or of character, means genuine and of proven quality.

clue.text: Who would prohibit the use of colour?

definitions.text: Who would prohibit the use of colour?

parts.words: Who would prohibit the use of colour?
parts.note: read as one who bans, and also as a flag, the colours a regiment or cause flies

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like a question about a censor forbidding colour; the answer is both someone who bans and a flag, since a flag is a display of colours.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a person who forbids things, and a flag or streamer bearing a design or slogan.

clue.text: Skill provided that routine result of human endeavour

parts.note: art means skill, as in the art of persuasion
if means provided that, on condition that
an act is a performer's routine

explanation.surface: Talent, if one's set performance is good, produces something made by people.
explanation.definitionFit: An artifact is an object made by human hands, as opposed to something natural.

clue.text: Acquisition by staff involved in corruption

indicators.note: involved in means the staff word is wrapped inside the corruption word

parts.note: attaint is an old word for a stain, taint or corruption
men are the staff or workforce

explanation.surface: A company takeover by employees caught up in bribery.
explanation.definitionFit: An attainment is something gained or achieved, an acquisition of skill or status.

clue.text: Qualification perhaps revised article containing loose end

indicators.note: containing means the rearranged article holds the other scrambled word within it
revised means the letters of article are rewritten in a new order
loose means the letters of end are set free and rearranged

explanation.surface: A journalist revises a piece that has a loose end left dangling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revised' turns ARTICLE into CRE...TIAL, and 'containing' puts DEN, from 'loose' end, inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A credential is evidence of competence; a qualification is one example, hence 'perhaps'.

clue.text: Revolution helping to suppress religious work

indicators.note: to suppress means hold down, so the religious work is held within the helping word

parts.note: a ration is a portion or helping
OT, the Old Testament, a religious book

explanation.surface: An uprising that aims to crush a sacred text.
explanation.definitionFit: A revolution is one complete turn about an axis, which is a rotation.

clue.text: Everyone intended to ignore first serious relationship

parts.note: all means everyone

indicators.note: to ignore first means the opening letter of the intended is dropped

parts.note: a fiance, one's intended, is the person one plans to marry

explanation.surface: Everybody meant to overlook their first serious love affair.
explanation.walkthrough: Intended looks like a verb, but it is a noun: one's intended is a fiance.
explanation.definitionFit: An alliance is a close union or bond, including a marriage between families.

clue.text: Low frequency noise in recording decayed

indicators.note: in means the noise is placed inside the recording

parts.note: CD, compact disc, is a recording
a rumble is a deep low-pitched sound

explanation.surface: A bass hum on an old recording that has deteriorated.
explanation.definitionFit: Crumbled means broke down into fragments, so decayed or disintegrated.

clue.text: Sportsman unlikely to run against British member of parliament and head of state

indicators.note: against means placed next to, so the pieces sit side by side

parts.note: fast colours are dyes that will not run in the wash
a parliament is the collective noun for owls, so one member is an owl
ER, Elizabeth Regina, the monarch who is the UK's head of state

explanation.surface: An athlete reluctant to stand for election against a British MP and the head of state.
explanation.walkthrough: Member of parliament is not an MP: a group of owls is a parliament. 'Unlikely to run' is fast in the sense of a dye that holds; ER is Elizabeth Regina.
explanation.definitionFit: A fast bowler is a cricketer who delivers the ball at high pace, so a sportsman.

clue.text: Broadcast removes restrictions on moratorium

indicators.note: broadcast means spoken over the air, so the word is taken by how it sounds

parts.note: frees means releases or removes restrictions on

explanation.surface: A news programme reports the lifting of a ban.
explanation.definitionFit: A freeze is a halt, as in a pay freeze, the same as a temporary suspension or moratorium.

clue.text: Raise last of very small steps partners could take

indicators.note: in a down entry raising a letter moves it upward, so the final letter shifts one place earlier

parts.note: minute means very small

explanation.surface: Dancers are urged to raise the final tiny step they take.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer, raising the last E of MINUTE lifts it one place above the T.
explanation.definitionFit: A minuet is a stately ballroom dance for couples, so a set of steps for partners.

clue.text: Relief as nutritionist recalled sandwiches likely to cause harm

indicators.note: recalled says the hidden letters are read backwards
sandwiches means the words hold the answer between them, as bread holds a filling

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A dietitian is relieved to recall sandwiches that could make people ill.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft put 'sandwiches' in the definition, but it is the signal that 'Relief as nutritionist' holds the letters; 'recalled' then reads them backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unsafe is dangerous, liable to cause injury or harm.

clue.text: Flaring up again having lost it in power

indicators.note: having lost means the word it is dropped from the longer word

parts.note: reigniting means catching fire again, flaring up again

explanation.surface: A conflict blazes up once more after losing its momentum among those who rule.
explanation.definitionFit: A reigning monarch or champion is the one currently holding the title or ruling.

clue.text: Love of cruelty in the modern era is encapsulated by Stalin and Mao primarily

indicators.note: encapsulated by means enclosed between the two initials
primarily means take the first letter of each of the two dictators' names

parts.note: AD, anno Domini, labels years of the modern era

explanation.surface: Cruelty in our age is summed up chiefly by two dictators.
explanation.definitionFit: Sadism is deriving pleasure from inflicting pain or humiliation on others.

clue.text: New cadet due to be trained

indicators.note: new means the letters of cadet due are made anew in a different order

explanation.surface: A fresh recruit at military academy is due to be drilled.
explanation.definitionFit: Educated means taught or schooled, which is to be trained in knowledge or skills.

clue.text: Remarkable apparatus for conveying information

definitions.meaning: first meaning: ... as an adjective, notable or striking, as in a ... achievement
second meaning: a device such as a railway ... that passes on information

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as praise for a clever gadget; the two stretches are separate meanings of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: Signal works as an adjective meaning conspicuous or notable and as a noun for a device giving information or instructions.

clue.text: Urgent request to have access controls

indicators.note: controls means holds in check, so the access word holds the other inside it

parts.note: entry means access, a way in
to have, as in have lunch, means to eat

explanation.surface: An insistent plea for permission to get in past security controls.
explanation.definitionFit: An entreaty is an earnest, pleading request or appeal.

clue.text: Quite popular and moving record?

parts.note: in means popular or fashionable
a deed is the legal document recording a transfer of property when you move house

explanation.surface: A hit song that is also emotionally touching.
explanation.walkthrough: Moving looks like touching, but here it is moving house, whose legal record is the title deed.
explanation.definitionFit: Said as an exclamation of agreement, 'Quite!' and 'Indeed!' are interchangeable.
